records.name: William F. Ganong
records.bio: Ganong was a botanist and Rudolf Blaschka’s field companion during the 1892 United States journey. Letters, specimens and travel records make him a key link between field observation in North America and the botanical work later carried out in Hosterwitz.

records.name: Alexander Goette
records.bio: Goette was a zoologist and university professor documented as an intermediary for Strasbourg’s 1890 order of Blaschka models. His record links institutional selection and commissioning to a specific university teaching collection.

records.name: George Lincoln Goodale
records.bio: Goodale, founding director of Harvard’s Botanical Museum, negotiated the botanical commission with Leopold and Rudolf. In this network he is both commissioner and scientific mediator, translating museum teaching needs into a sustained workshop programme.

records.name: Philip Henry Gosse
records.bio: Gosse’s published marine zoology, especially his richly illustrated work on sea anemones, belongs to the visual and scientific source environment of early Blaschka zoological models. He is included here as a source-author rather than as a documented buyer or workshop correspondent.

records.name: Albert C. L. G. Günther
records.bio: Günther was a zoologist at the British Museum and appears in the museum-side history of Blaschka holdings. The project uses his record to connect departmental custody, correspondence and collection administration rather than treating the museum as a single impersonal recipient.

records.name: Julius von Haast
records.bio: Haast, geologist and director of Canterbury Museum, appears in the Australasian correspondence and collection network surrounding Blaschka models. His inclusion here follows documented institutional and commercial links rather than general scientific acquaintance.

records.name: Ernst Haeckel
records.bio: Haeckel’s published zoological descriptions and illustrations form part of the scientific and visual environment against which some Blaschka model designs can be studied. He is included as a source-author; the project does not turn that published relationship into an undocumented personal collaboration.

records.name: James Hector
records.bio: Hector was a scientist and museum director in New Zealand whose correspondence intersects the Otago and Hutton collection network. In the People index he functions as an institutional node within the broader Australasian circulation of natural-history objects.

records.name: Thomas Holbein Hendley
records.bio: Hendley, a surgeon and museum organiser in Jaipur, was the honorary secretary and order organiser in the 1886–1887 Jeypore Blaschka transaction. Workshop correspondence lets the project follow his order through manufacture, payment, cases and the Trieste–Bombay route.
